faq.a: The World Health Organization lists compulsive sexual behaviour disorder in the ICD-11. It describes an ongoing pattern of not being able to control strong, repeated sexual urges.

A 90-day detox, also called sexual sobriety or abstinence, is a common step in sex addiction recovery. It gives you space to heal, figure out your triggers, and build new ways to cope. The goal is to reset unhealthy patterns and work toward healthy intimacy, not to give up sex forever. Plan it with your therapist, and talk it through with your partner if you're in a relationship.

faq.q: What does "disclosure is better than discovery" mean?
faq.a: Telling the truth yourself, ideally with help from a therapist, does less damage than your partner finding out on their own. When they find out on their own, they're hurt by the behavior and by the hiding.

faq.q: What should I do when an urge hits?
faq.a: Make a safety plan, reach out to someone, and check HALT: are you hungry, angry, lonely, or tired? Then wait it out. Give it 15 minutes and go for a walk.

faq.q: Where can I find a support group?
faq.a: The Sex Addiction group sessions on BetterHelp are one option. You need a BetterHelp membership to join, and this site isn't affiliated with BetterHelp or the group. Sex and Love Addicts Anonymous (SLAA) is another option.

faq.q: I was hurt by my partner. Is any of this for me?
faq.a: Yes. Betrayal hurts, and your healing matters on its own. Pick "I was hurt" at the top of this page to see resources for you. You can also ask your partner to go to their group, take notes, and share them with you after.
